about.title: Hawaiian Gardens Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Hawaiian Gardens is a compact Los Angeles County city, but its households rely on the same everyday products as anywhere else — appliances, tools, vehicle parts, medical devices, and consumer goods bought locally or online. When one of these products fails and causes harm, California's strict liability rules can work in the injured person's favor: you generally don't need to prove the manufacturer was negligent, only that the product had a defect and that defect caused your injury. That said, these cases often involve multiple potentially responsible parties, from the manufacturer to a distributor to the retailer who sold it near Carson Street or elsewhere in town. Preserving the product exactly as it was when it failed matters a great deal for any later evaluation. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself, but we can connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney in California who evaluates these claims and works on contingency — meaning no fee unless there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: What to Know About Product Liability Claims in California

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Burden
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability, you generally don't have to prove the manufacturer was careless — just that a defect existed and caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which can widen the pool of parties an attorney may look at.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: Keeping the item in its post-incident condition, rather than discarding or repairing it, can be important for an attorney to properly assess what happened.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Under California's strict liability approach, you typically need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, not that the company was careless in making it. An attorney can review your specific situation to see how this applies.

items.question: I bought the product from a small shop in Hawaiian Gardens, not directly from the manufacturer. Can I still make a claim?
items.answer: Possibly. Retailers and distributors, along with manufacturers, can sometimes share liability for a defective product under California law. An independent attorney can look at where you purchased the item and who else may be involved.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep it exactly as it was after the incident, without repairing, cleaning, or discarding it. This preservation can matter for any later review of the defect. If you're unsure how to store it safely, an attorney can advise you.

items.question: Is there a cost to get connected with an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and attorneys in our network generally work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover money. There's no obligation to move forward after you're connected.
